newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Indian PM accepts Mandela invitation to S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM accepts Mandela invitation to S.Africa.

text.p: New Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has accepted an invitation by President Nelson Mandela to pay a state visit South Africa, Mandela's spokeswoman said on Thursday.

"An invitation has been extended to him to come to South Africa on a state visit as a guest of the state president. He has accepted and a date is to be confirmed soon," spokeswoman Priscilla Naidoo told Reuters.

South Africa and India have close historic links which are to be commemorated on Friday when Mandela posthumously awards the Freedom of the City of Pietermaritzburg to India's independence leader Mahatma Gandhi.
Gandhi was a leading campaigner for racial equality in South Africa early in the century.

His first brush with racism was at the Pietermaritzburg Station 103 years ago when he was evicted from a first-class train compartment reserved for whites. He later said that the experience had changed the course of his life.
Mandela, who has visited India three times, said in New Delhi last month that he expected annual bilateral trade with India to pass $2 billion in the next three years.
Indo-South African trade touched $220 million in 1994/95 (April-March) and had reached $260 million in the first half of 1995/96, officials said.
Gujral's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in parliament on Tuesday.
